statement.p: The moment of inertia of a solid body about an axis in 3-space relates the angular acceleration about this axis to torque (force twisting the body). The moments of inertia about the coordinate axes of a body of constant density and mass m occupying a region W of volume V are defined to be I_x = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (y^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_y = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_z = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+y^2) \,dV
Use these definitions to find the moment of inertia about the z-axis of the rectangular solid of mass 120 given by 0 \le x \le 3, 0 \le y \le 5, 0 \le z \le 4.

static.solution:
V of the solid is 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 = 60. Thus for I_x we have I_x = \frac{120}{60}\int_W\, y^2 + z^2\,dV = 2\int_0^3\int_0^5\int_0^4\,y^2 + z^2\,dz\,dy\,dx. This is I_x = 2\int_0^3\int_0^5 y^2 z + \frac13 z^3\bigg|_{z=0}^{z=4} = 2\int_0^{3}\int_0^{5}\, 4 y^2 + \frac{64}{3}\, dy\,dx, or I_x = 2\int_0^3 \frac{500}{3} + \frac{320}{3}\, dx = 1640.
Similarly, I_y = 1000,\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad I_z = 1360.
